neighbours.label: the adverb ' fully' (and similar completeness adverbs) before a participle or adjective ('fully formed', 'fully open access')
fire: The new bridge will be fully open to traffic by June.
Make sure the chicken is fully cooked before serving it.
The hospital is now fully staffed after months of shortages.
Our records show the loan was fully repaid in 2019.
The battery takes three hours to become fully charged.
Each apartment comes fully furnished with a washer and dryer.
The vaccine is fully approved for adults over eighteen.
Wait until the paint is fully dry before you hang the picture.
